transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-09-18 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Lena (Redwood AE), Rahul (Redwood SE), Arielle (Redwood CSM), Daniel (Elm Vale CTO), Mina (Lead SRE), Ethan (Data Eng), Sofia (Product)

Summary: Quick implementation kickoff to align staging access, pilot goals, and initial performance checks. Customer is leaning toward a private/Dedicated evaluation for latency-sensitive pipelines but wants a cost comparison. Action items and next steps agreed at the end.

Topics: staging VPC, data residency, pilot scope, perf benchmarks, roll-forward plan, success criteria (latency <120ms p95 for core API), RBAC/SSO.

[00:00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, uh thanks for joining on a Friday, appreciate it. quick intro — I'm Lena, AE. with me Rahul our solutions engineer and Arielle who will be your CSM through onboarding.
[00:00:18] Daniel: Thanks Lena. we have a hard stop at 14:50 UTC for an internal sync but otherwise good. quick note we want to get staging live before end of month so timing is tight.
[00:00:36] Rahul: Great. i'll try to keep the tech parts crisp. can you confirm the pilot scope — is it inference for customer support routing and embeddings indexing for search?
[00:00:50] Sofia: Yeah primarily routing and a smaller embeddings workload for search similarity. we'll run it behind the new microservice and test latency under steady load.
[00:01:10] Mina: also we care about data egress and logs, we need to keep logs in our account, and audit trails — SOC2 is in play for us.
[00:01:28] Arielle: noted. we'll include audit log retention and SSO steps in the runbook.

[00:03:05] Lena: Okay onboarding wise, two paths: Hosted (fastest) or Dedicated / Private. from what you said, looks like Dedicated makes sense for isolation, correct?
[00:03:22] Daniel: We're leaning there, yeah. Latency is critical, and we'd like predictable throughput. but we need the cost delta.
[00:03:40] Rahul: for Dedicated we can reserve a pool and pin model versions. There's also autoscale/burst for short spikes. i can run numbers on unit cost vs hosted — do you have target qps?
[00:03:55] Ethan: For phase 1 it's small, like 8-12 qps average with 100 tokens per request typical. p95 latency target is under 120ms for the routing call.
[00:04:14] Rahul: 120ms p95 is tight; depends on model and quantization. with a trimmed model variant and proper batching config we can approach that on a Dedicated nv4-class setup. but we'll validate with a perf harness.

[00:06:00] [Speaker 1]: (murmur) can we talk about VPC?
[00:06:05] Mina: yes VPC peering is necessary, and KMS integration for keys. we also want to put the inference nodes in our subnet so traffic doesn't traverse public internet.
[00:06:25] Lena: that's supported via Private deployment; we have a VPC-onboarding checklist. i'll send the network diagram template.
[00:06:40] Arielle: we'll need an IAM/service account and the minimum ports opened — i'll put the template in the follow-up.

[00:08:12] Daniel: compliance — we're SOC2 Type II; do you have SOC documents and pen-test reports?
[00:08:25] Arielle: yes, we have a SOC2 pack and our security whitepaper. i'll share the links, and we can schedule a short security handoff with your InfoSec.
[00:08:42] Mina: and ISO/other regs?
[00:08:47] Arielle: ISO is in progress; our audit logs and KMS flows are documented in the security pack.

[00:10:30] Rahul: on implementation sequencing: step 1 — staging networking and access; step 2 — model selection and quantization profile; step 3 — perf bench runs with sample prompt set; step 4 — iterate. we'll put the runbook in the repo.
[00:10:48] Ethan: for model selection, are you recommending open models or Redwood curated variants?
[00:11:00] Rahul: For latency vs cost we usually start with a smaller open variant Redwood-verified, then if you need better quality we can try a hybrid or higher-capacity pinned model. backlog: we want to avoid large context lengths in the pilot.

[00:12:35] [00:12:35] Daniel: any gotchas on KV cache or stateful calls?
[00:12:42] Rahul: KV cache is handled by the runtime, but patterns that create unique prefixes reduce cache effectiveness. we recommend batching, consistent prefixing, and a small TTL for session vectors. (note: transcription sometimes says K-V cash)

[00:15:05] Lena: i'll summarize responsibilities: Redwood sends onboarding checklist + SOC pack. Elm Vale sends infra diagram, IAM role, and expected QPS. Redwood runs a perf harness and shares results.
[00:15:22] Mina: yes and we'll provide logs retention requirements. Also need SSO/SAML for team access.
[00:15:35] Arielle: SAML is supported; i'll send the SSO integration guide and metadata endpoint details.

[00:17:50] Daniel: curious about fallback policies; if Dedicated capacity drops, can requests failover to Hosted?
[00:18:00] Rahul: yes, we support smart routing and fallback. you'd set policies to route to Hosted-compatible variants. there is a cost implication but it's seamless for uptime.
[00:18:20] Ethan: ok good. we need to test failover during the pilot.

[00:20:10] Lena: on telemetry — the console provides per-route latency and token cost. are those sufficient for your SRE dashboarding?
[00:20:25] Mina: yes if we can get per-route p95 and token breakdowns exported. we prefer Prometheus scrape endpoints or daily CSV exports.
[00:20:40] Rahul: we have metrics export and alert hooks; i'll add the link to metric docs.

[00:23:05] [00:23:05] Sofia: quick question on embeddings indexing — do you recommend storing vectors in your system or our vector DB?
[00:23:20] Rahul: both patterns are used. For isolation and performance, many customers store embeddings in their own DB and call the embedding endpoint. Redwood can host embedding generation in Dedicated so vectors never leave your VPC.
[00:23:38] Mina: that's important — we'd prefer generation within our VPC and store locally.

[00:26:00] Daniel: timeline check: if onboarding checklist goes out today, when can you run benchmarks?
[00:26:10] Rahul: assuming we get infra access and a small test dataset by 2026-09-22, i can run a perf harness and share results by 2026-09-24.
[00:26:30] Arielle: and we'll have the security pack and SSO guide shared by 2026-09-20.

[00:29:00] [Speaker 2]: (overlap) about pricing model — is there a simple comparison doc?
[00:29:05] Lena: yes we'll share a Dedicated vs Hosted cost spreadsheet with example qps scenarios.
[00:29:18] Daniel: can you include billing cadence and reserved commit options?
[00:29:25] Lena: yes.

[00:31:40] Rahul: technical note on batching — to meet latency SLO we may use small batch sizes and prefix caching; for embeddings batches can be larger. i'll include recommended settings in the perf report.
[00:31:58] Mina: are there recommended quantization profiles? we have some int8 experiments internally.
[00:32:08] Rahul: we can recommend quant profiles and run quality checks against your eval prompts. sometimes int8 works fine for routing tasks. we'll report any regressions.

[00:35:00] Sofia: stakeholder map — who should be on the pilot check-ins?
[00:35:08] Arielle: recommend weekly 30m with product, sres, and redwood se/csm. we'll propose recurring invites.

[00:37:20] [00:37:20] Daniel: anything else from your side?
[00:37:25] Lena: just to confirm next steps: we'll send the onboarding pack, SOC docs, cost spreadsheet; Rahul will prep perf harness and a sample prompt set; Arielle will send access templates and SSO guide.
[00:37:45] Mina: we'll send infra diagram and expected qps by 2026-09-22.

[00:40:10] Rahul: small aside — competitors you mentioned earlier (Anthropic/AWS Bedrock) often trade off latency with model quality and ecosystem integrations; we'll highlight those in the cost/feature doc.

[00:42:00] Lena: quick recap and owners — Arielle, you capture action items and circulate. we'll aim to regroup on 2026-09-25 for the pilot runbook and first perf run.
[00:42:18] Arielle: noted.
[00:45:50] Daniel: ok thanks all. let's keep the comms tight, appreciate the clear asks.
[00:46:00] Lena: thanks everyone, talk soon.

End of transcript.
